literal: Those who value the true substance will not embrace the mean pleasure, [as do] those of wisdom who seek the wealth of grace.
translation: Those who value the true substance of life and those of wisdom who seek the wealth of grace will never embrace the mean pleasure of prostitutes.
modern: உண்மையான நற்பண்புகளை மதிப்போரும், அருளாகிய உயர்ந்த செல்வத்தை ஆராயும் அறிவுடையோரும், விலைமகளிரின் இழிவான இன்பத்தைப் பொருந்த மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet explains that individuals with true wisdom and moral clarity will not fall for the mercenary affection of prostitutes. The poet uses the term 'punnalam' (mean or worthless pleasure) to describe the superficial intimacy bought with money, which lacks genuine love. Those who value 'poruḷ' (the true substance or virtue of life) and those who seek 'aruṭporuḷ' (the wealth of grace) possess a refined understanding that naturally guards them against such degrading traps. True intellectual and spiritual maturity elevates a person above base, commercialized lust.
